newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent futures lower on Iraq oil exports.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent futures lower on Iraq oil exports.

text.p: SIMEX Brent crude futures settled lower late Monday with the market sentiment depressed on news of the imminent Iraqi oil exports from Tuesday, brokers said.
February contract was last traded at $23.45 per barrel, five cents off its intraday high with a total of 66 lots seen traded. The contract last closed at $23.78 on London's IPE on Friday.
January was last traded at $24.20 with only 3 lots changed hands. It last closed at $24.54 in London.
Iraq oil minister, Amir Muhammed Rasheed was reported as saying on Friday that Iraq expects to be able to resume oil exports from 0500 GMT on Tuesday.
"There were also disccussions that the Iraqi-Turkey oil pipeline will also be opened within this week," one broker said.
Brokers said while news of Iraqi oil coming to the market has mostly been factored in, prices were still expected to be under pressure.
Under the oil-for-food plan, Iraq is allowed to export up to $2 billion worth of oil in exchange for food and humanitarian aid.
